system.description:
Origins

Many societies consider halflings small, lazy criminals and lump them together with rats and other pests living on the edges of the city. Somehow they got aboard spelljammers, and now they turn up wherever something is happening, ready to lift a purse or scavenge anything useful while nobody watches.

Most halflings are insular and see little of the wider world, preferring a comfortable chair, as many meals as the day allows and a nap afterwards. Even heroic halflings tend to have simple wishes — good food, friends and family — and homesickness is the ailment that most often troubles those who travel.

Appearance

Halflings are among the smallest thinking beings of the Great Wheel, about half a human's size. They look mostly human, but with slightly odd, childlike proportions and features and ears that are pointed, if not as long as an elf's. Their skin tones span the human range, though most people just call it 'dirty', and clean halflings are rare: they sit so low in the societies around them that survival leaves no time for such concerns.

Hair and eyes run to earthy tones with hints of colour — muddy reds and blondes, and hazel eyes that shift between green and brown. Many dye and cut their hair in outrageous styles, both to be noticed and to show which gang or family they belong to.

In Play

Halflings live in the gutters and slums of their 'betters', largely ignored, yet they have a surprisingly rich culture built on loyalty and sacrifice for friends and family. Once a halfling commits to something or trusts someone, only dire need will make them break that bond. They shun informers and traitors and often take justice into their own hands; a halfling who talks too much to the Harmonium tends to end up in the morgue.

They hold the larger races — nearly everyone — in contempt and lie to, cheat and rob them without remorse, since those races never cut them any slack. They rarely go among them except to scavenge, and most never notice the half-scale cities growing beneath their feet or in forgotten cargo holds, full of all the things that went missing. Opportunists at heart, halflings always take the path of least effort, and that path is usually a cheat; very few want a fair fight.

Example heroes (p. 46): Coerg, Wheeler, Captain Selphie.

power.name: Shifty
power.description: A Halfling's Static Defense is 10 + 6 × Dexterity − 2 × Size, replacing the usual formula based on Dexterity and Wisdom.
